The Cartesian plane: The x-axis and y-axis meet at the origin. A point is an ordered pair (x, y): abscissa first, ordinate second.
Quadrants and signs: The four quadrants differ in the signs of x and y. Points on the axes belong to no quadrant.
Plotting points and reading coordinates: Plot a point by moving along x and then along y. Distances from the axes are the absolute values of the coordinates.
Reflection, distance and midpoint: Reflections change signs of coordinates. Lengths along axes are differences; the midpoint averages the coordinates.
